docs.summary: The project file a build generates, as data.
docs.remarks:
Generating a csproj is legitimate, because a csproj is a data file and it is what carries `PublishAot`, `PublishTrimmed` and the runtime identifiers. Generating program source is not, which is why the player is a compiled project instead.

A new platform describes its project by filling this in rather than assembling XML by hand, which is the difference between adding a target and reimplementing the desktop pipeline.

docs.summary: The SDK to use for the project. Defaults to Microsoft.NET.Sdk.

members.name: TargetFramework
members.signature: public required string TargetFramework { get; init; }

docs.summary: The target framework moniker for the project, for example net8.0.

Plural, because several real targets are not one architecture: an Android bundle carries multiple ABIs and a macOS universal binary is merged from two. One emits the singular property, several emit the plural one, which is what the SDK expects.

Files to embed as resources in the compiled assembly.
Renders the project file. Every group is sorted, so an unchanged build produces an identical file whatever order the caller collected things in, and every value is escaped.
